# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

blocks.text:
content.js
embed_relay.js
# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". # gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

---

Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". The Apps tab is in the Flutter app (flutter_app). Let me check the flutter_app structure and how the Apps tab / apps grid is shown.

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

blocks.text:
content.js
embed_relay.js
# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". The Apps tab is in the Flutter app (flutter_app). Let me check the flutter_app structure and how the Apps tab / apps grid is shown.

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". The Apps tab is in the Flutter app (flutter_app). Let me check the flutter_app structure and how the Apps tab / apps grid is shown.

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

content.js
embed_relay.js
# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". # gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

content.js

# fa — browser agent extension

The extension hosts THE fa web experience: the same Flutter web app users
know from the main page runs in the side panel (and as a full tab from the
toolbar), and on top of it the agent gets the full Chrome extension API
surface as tools — tabs, windows, history, bookmarks, downloads, cookies,
and first-class JavaScript injection into pages. One sentence: fa-for-web
moves into the extension and grows browser superpowers. The embedded agent
core is Dart, compiled with dart2js by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh`;
plain JavaScript classic scripts around it — no npm.

## Two panel modes

`panel/panel.html` is an app-hosting bootstrap:

- **App panel** — when `browser_ext/app/` exists (built by
  `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app`), the panel loads the real fa
  web app from local extension assets (MV3 CSP-compliant, no remote code).
- **Legacy fallback chat** — without `app/`, the v1 minimal chat UI
  (pairing, provider form, approvals, event log) is shown instead. It
  stays as fallback only.

Status note: the app-hosting panel currently runs the app's own local
agent path when hosted; the service-worker protocol server is ready for
it, the app-side worker-relay chat integration is still pending (see
[docs/browser-extension.md](../docs/browser-extension.md) → Status).

## Build & load (unpacked)

1. Build the zip:

   ```bash
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh             # agent only
   bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app  # + the real app UI in the panel
   ```

   The script compiles the Dart agent (when a Dart SDK is on PATH) and
   zips the runtime files into `build/fa-extension.zip`. `--with-app`
   first runs `flutter build web --release` and bundles the result as
   `browser_ext/app/` (a build artifact, never committed).

2. Open `chrome://extensions`, enable **Developer mode**.
3. **Load unpacked** → select this `browser_ext/` directory — or drag in /
   load `build/fa-extension.zip`.

Minimum Chrome 116. Manifest: 26 core permissions, the 9 second-tier
APIs in `optional_permissions` (registered-hidden behind a Settings
gate), and `<all_urls>` in `optional_host_permissions` for store
builds — per-permission justifications:
[docs/browser-extension-permissions.md](../docs/browser-extension-permissions.md).

## Where keys live

The provider API key and all agent config live in
`chrome.storage.local` **inside the service worker** and are read only
there — never in content scripts, never in page worlds, never in the
panel. In extension mode the UI process holds no keys and makes no
provider fetches; everything flows over an extension-internal
`chrome.runtime` port.

## What the agent can do — 34 tools

| Family | Tools | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs (9) | `tabs_open` `tabs_close` `tabs_update` `tabs_query` `tabs_move` `tabs_group` `tabs_ungroup` `tabs_reload` `tabs_discard` | query = read; rest = write |
| Windows (4) | `windows_open` `windows_update` `windows_close` `windows_list` | list = read; rest = write |
| Groups (2) | `groups_update` `groups_close` | write |
| Sessions (2) | `sessions_recent` `sessions_restore` | read / write |
| History (1) | `history_search` | read |
| Bookmarks (4) | `bookmarks_list` `bookmarks_add` `bookmarks_update` `bookmarks_remove` | list = read; rest = write |
| Downloads (3) | `downloads_start` `downloads_search` `downloads_cancel` | search = read; rest = write |
| Cookies (3) | `cookies_get` `cookies_set` `cookies_remove` | get = read; rest = write |
| Injection & CDP (4) | `inject_js` `inject_css` `cdp_eval` `page_screenshot` | inject_js = exec and **always prompts** (MAIN world); inject_css = write; cdp_eval / page_screenshot = exec |
| App & navigation (2) | `app_screenshot` `nav_wait` | read |

Restricted pages (chrome://, Chrome Web Store, extension pages, PDF
viewer) are never scripted or injected; tab management (open/close/move)
still works there so the agent can clean up.

## Entry points

The extension panel hosts the Flutter web app. The Apps tab is part of the Flutter app. The ticket references `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` and "browser_ext Apps tab". The Apps tab is in the Flutter app (flutter_app). Let me check the flutter_app structure and how the Apps tab / apps grid is shown.
