blocks.text:
## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

**Capability rules (issue #1079, host-wiring SDK layer):** every NEW
host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven
hosts (`cli`, `macos`, `ios`, `android`, `web`, `extension`, `outlook`) a
state: `on`, `off(reason)`, or `transport(choice, reason)` for a
partial/different transport. The record types, validation and transport
vocabularies live in `lib/src/hosts/host_capability_profile.dart`; the
seven built-in profiles — where those per-host cells are actually
declared — live in `lib/src/hosts/host_wiring_builder.dart`. The
matrix-completeness test rejects undeclared capabilities, so "CLI got X,
app didn't" cannot happen silently. A capability that is
`off` is INVISIBLE: hidden from the host's UI (menus, settings, slash
commands, tool palettes) AND from everything model-facing (tool schemas,
system-prompt sections, skills listings, help) — the agent never sees
what it cannot use and the user never sees a button that errors; on a
`transport` cell only the available transports surface. Profiles can only
NARROW what the platform floor allows: force-enabling a floored
capability throws `HostProfileViolation` at construction, never a runtime
surprise.

**Host shells wire through the builder (issue #1079 slice 2):** a host
constructs its agent stack via `wireAgentCore` (lib/src/hosts/
host_agent_wiring.dart) — typed `AgentCoreServices` in, `WiredAgentCore`
(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9). The
flutter_app is the second shell (slice 5): it wires through
`flutterAppHostProfile` (lib/src/hosts/app_host_profile.dart — the app
host's own honest today-state, not the built-ins, whose cells pin the
matrix TARGET) and packages its platform tool families as a declared
`app-platform` extension — per-platform conditioning stays construction
glue in the shell, never a bare `if` around registration. Capabilities
the builder registers no tool for are declared with PRESENCE MARKER
services (`dynamicMessageSink`, `onDeviceProviderFactory`, the
`extRuntimeFactory` precedent): the host's extension carries the tool,
the marker keeps the cell honestly wired instead of run-narrowing off.
A host whose session scope differs from `ExecutionEnv.cwd` (the app's
mounted project folders) passes `sessionCwd` so the fabric groups mail by
workspace.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and

Very important context on the host capability matrix (issue #1079): "every NEW host-wiring capability declares its matrix state AT BIRTH — for all seven hosts". But that's for agent-facing capabilities/tools. The unpacked-loader is a UI feature of the app, not an agent tool — likely doesn't need the capability matrix. ## Implementation plan

### 1. `UnpackedWidgetLoader` (flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart)
Pure Dart over `ExecutionEnv` — the load pipeline: files map → validate → store. Reuses `AppsStore.installWidget` for the write (same shape — I1), but with origin `unpacked` (I3). Validation via the shared validator:

**Shared validator**: the ticket says the validator is shared with #1614's storage reads. #1614 isn't in the repo; the shared rule engine that EXISTS is `fa_widgets_tool` (used by publish pre-flight, issue #1045: "a manifest that passes on-device passes in CI, with byte-identical error strings"). The unpacked loader should use THE SAME engine — following the `WidgetPublishService` pattern (materialize to temp dir on VM; manifest-level fallback on web). Wait — but there's a wrinkle: `fa_widgets_tool`'s `validateWidgetDirectory` requires manifest id == folder name, and the materialized folder name = id. That works.

But hold on — for unpacked loads, do we want catalog-CI-identical strictness? The catalog validator requires e.g. `version` strict semver, `minRuntime` checks, id==folder. Chrome-parity: unpacked = local folder load. If the local folder has a weird version, should the load fail? The ticket AC2: "invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest)". The core validation: id regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence. The fa_widgets_tool engine gives exactly these plus more (semver strictness...). Hmm, semver strictness might be stricter than needed but it IS the shared ruleset — "the same validator" is the invariant. Consistency wins: use the fa_widgets engine.

But there's a catch: the fa_widgets_tool engine is `dart:io`-based. On web it throws UnsupportedError → manifest-level fallback (the same pattern as `_manifestLevelValidatorIssues`). The web fallback still validates: id regex, manifest schema (via WidgetManifest.decode), entry presence (files map). Let me read the rest of `_manifestLevelValidatorIssues` to reuse it.

Also — do I validate BEFORE writing anything (all-or-nothing)? Yes: validate the in-memory files first; only then write via installWidget (which itself is write-verified, all-or-nothing-ish).

**Where should the loader live?** `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`. It must not import dart:io directly...? flutter_app/lib already has dart:io imports (widget_publish_service.dart). But following the existing pattern, put the dart:io-touching validator run behind the same try/catch UnsupportedError pattern. Actually the loader service itself can be pure (env + files map) and delegate validation to a `UnpackedWidgetValidator` that follows the publish-service pattern.

### 2. Provenance (I3)
`.installed.json` already carries `origin` per app ('catalog'). Add `'unpacked'` origin. `AppsStore.installWidget` hardcodes `entry['origin'] = 'catalog'`. I'll add an `origin` parameter (default 'catalog') — minimal change — or a dedicated `installUnpackedWidget` method that records origin 'unpacked'. JsAppInfo: add `installSource` (null = not recorded / created by agent; 'catalog' | 'unpacked'). listApps reads `.installed.json` — hmm, listApps doesn't currently read installed meta per app... it does `_readInstalled()` for pruning. I can attach installSource in listApps from the installed meta. Surfacing in UI: catalog sheet "Created by me" section / tile menu. Minimal: show a small badge in the launcher tile menu + catalog sheet. Let me keep UI surfacing modest but real: in `WidgetsCatalogSheet._buildCreatedByMe` show provenance chip ("unpacked"), and in the launcher tile long-press menu show source. Hmm, but scope... I3 says "apps carry an install source (catalog | unpacked), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder)".

### 3. UI: "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab
- `AppsPanel` ("My Apps"): add a "Load unpacked" action next to "Get widgets" — opens the folder picker (web) → confirm dialog (name, version, declared capabilities — network fetch + commands, E2/exfiltration gate) → load → refresh grid. On replace-existing-id: explicit confirm dialog.

The AppsPanel is the "My Apps" right panel. AppLauncherScreen is the mobile/home launcher. To cover the "Apps tab" in both shapes, put the shared load flow in a helper (showUnpackedLoadSheet or a function used by both). Simplest: add the "Load unpacked" button to BOTH the AppsPanel (next to "Get widgets") and the launcher (tile menu or tab row?). Hmm — keep it focused: AppsPanel + launcher tile-add area. Actually let me check what the extension panel app shows: FA_HOST=extension — does it boot WideLayoutShell? Let me check main.dart briefly for the extension host.

### 4. Restart persistence (AC3)
Free via env (OPFS/IndexedDB snapshot of the memory FS — the same layer catalog installs already use). IT test: MemoryExecutionEnv → load → new AppsStore over a fresh MemoryExecutionEnv replayed... Actually "re-open env" = create a second AppsStore over a fresh env with the same snapshot restored, then listApps shows the app and it boots. The persistent-web-env has restore tests; for the IT I can use MemoryExecutionEnv + simulate restart by re-reading. Actually simplest honest IT: write to env A, snapshot it (FsSnapshotExporter?) — overkill. The memory env IS the env; a restart = new AppsStore over the SAME env contents. The catalog install already has such coverage. I'll do: load → dispose store → new AppsStore over same env → listApps → boot entry assembly works. That covers "stored exactly like a catalog app, boot needs zero special cases" (I1) and restart persistence at the unit level.

### 5. Size cap (E4)
Cap on widget.js (e.g. 2 MiB?) — fa_widgets validator warns >1MiB but doesn't error. For unpacked load, ticket E4: "huge widget.js → size cap with clear message". I'll enforce a hard cap in the loader (e.g. 2 MiB per file / 5 MiB total? The catalog warns at 5 MiB total). Choose: per-file cap 2 MiB with named error, matching the entry-size cap the catalog uses as error? Hmm — validator warns >1MiB, and there's `sizeWarnBytes = 5MB`. For the unpacked loader, a hard cap protects OPFS quota. I'll implement: total package cap 10 MiB, per-file cap 2 MiB → named error `file too large`. That's loader-level (not part of the shared validator, which stays catalog-identical).

### 6. E1 — folder deleted before load completes → honest error
With the files-map input the loader is atomic (files already read into memory), so "folder deleted before load completes" manifests at PICK time (user picks empty/no files → error "no files chosen") or read failure at pick → surface as named error. In the web picker: if no manifest.json found in picked files → named error "manifest.json not found in the picked folder". That's the honest-error path.

- Folder name (after root strip) must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` (validator's rule id == folder name covers this; but I need to map the picked folder to the id FIRST: the id comes from the manifest; the folder in the env becomes `apps/<manifest.id>`. The fa_widgets rule "manifest id must equal folder name" applies to the picked top folder name; if a user picked a folder named "My Widget" with id "my-widget", catalog rules would reject. Chrome-parity: the picked folder name shouldn't matter — the id lives in the manifest. Hmm. But the ticket says "id regex, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator". The fa_widgets engine's folder-name rule would reject a "My Widget" named folder. For unpacked loading, the app-store folder is `apps/<id>` created BY us from manifest.id — the picked folder's own name is irrelevant (it's not a catalog submission).

So: strict catalog-engine validation would be WRONG for the folder-name rule (Chrome loads a folder named anything; the id comes from the manifest). Also semver strictness: catalog requires strict X.Y.Z — an unpacked worktree with version "1.0" would fail... The JsAppInfo defaults version '1.0.0'. Hmm.

Decision: the shared validator for unpacked loads validates exactly what the ticket lists:
1. **id** `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` (bad id → named error) + traversal-safe (no `.`/`/`/`..` — the regex already excludes those).
2. **manifest schema** — via `WidgetManifest.fromJson` (the engine's parser: byte-identical errors, shared with #1045's client and CI).
3. **entry presence** — `widget.js` non-empty in the files map (and the manifest-declared tile entry, if any).

Where the catalog engine ADDS value without risk (version semver, minRuntime), an unpacked dev folder shouldn't be blocked — dev iteration on a worktree is the whole point. Design: `flutter_app/lib/apps/widget_validator.dart`:
```dart
class WidgetPayloadIssue { final String code; final String message; }
class WidgetPayloadValidator {
  // validates a files-map payload {relPath: bytes} against the widget contract:
  // manifest.json present + parses (WidgetManifest.fromJson — shared engine), 
  // id matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$, widget.js present + non-empty,
  // declared tile entry present, size caps.
  static ValidatedWidgetPayload? validate(Map<String, Uint8List> files)
}
```
Pure Dart (no dart:io) — works on web + VM, fully unit-testable (UT-*). Uses `fa_widgets_tool`'s `WidgetManifest` parser (the shared schema engine) but NOT the directory-walking validator (dart:io, folder-name rule — wrong for unpacked). Now I have everything I need for the loader design. Let me also check the `apps_catalog_tool.dart` — the agent-facing tool that installs catalog widgets. Maybe unpacked loading should ALSO be agent-accessible? The ticket open question 2: "Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? Default: second tier." — so NO for this leg (second tier, default deferred). Good — keep the loader UI-only.

Now let me check `AppPermissions`'s network and the confirm content: the exfiltration gate shows "this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765". The manifest's network is a boolean; the origins come from the code? The ticket's exfiltration gate language ("a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time") — with the actual schema being `network: true` (any origin), the honest display is "network access: yes (jsr.fetchJson any origin)" + declared allowedCommands. E2 says "manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it)". With the schema as-is, showing the network capability flag satisfies "the confirmation lists it". I'll surface `network` + `allowedCommands` in the confirm.

Now — where does the confirm get the network list? From the manifest parse. `WidgetManifest.network` (bool), `allowedCommands` (list).

### Size cap (E4)
Loader cap: per-file 2 MiB, total 8 MiB? The catalog warn thresholds: file >1MiB warn, sizeWarnBytes 5MiB total warn. For unpacked: hard errors — I'll use 2 MiB per file and 8 MiB total with clear named errors. Hmm, actually let me keep it simple and aligned: per-file cap 2 MiB (widget.js + assets), total package cap 10 MiB. Fine.

### Id regex & traversal
- Folder name (after root strip) must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` (validator's rule id == folder name covers this; but I need to map the picked folder to the id FIRST: the id comes from the manifest; the folder in the env becomes `apps/<manifest.id>`. The fa_widgets rule "manifest id must equal folder name" applies to the picked top folder name; if a user picked a folder named "My Widget" with id "my-widget", catalog rules would reject. Chrome-parity: the picked folder name shouldn't matter — the id lives in the manifest. Hmm. But the ticket says "id regex, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator". The fa_widgets engine's folder-name rule would reject a "My Widget" named folder. For unpacked loading, the app-store folder is `apps/<id>` created BY us from manifest.id — the picked folder's own name is irrelevant (it's not a catalog submission).

So: strict catalog-engine validation would be WRONG for the folder-name rule (Chrome loads a folder named anything; the id comes from the manifest). Also semver strictness: catalog requires strict X.Y.Z — an unpacked worktree with version "1.0" would fail... The JsAppInfo defaults version '1.0.0'. Hmm.

Decision: the shared validator for unpacked loads validates exactly what the ticket lists:
1. **id** `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` (bad id → named error) + traversal-safe (no `.`/`/`/`..` — the regex already excludes those).
2. **manifest schema** — via `WidgetManifest.fromJson` (the engine's parser: byte-identical errors, shared with #1045's client and CI).
3. **entry presence** — `widget.js` non-empty in the files map (and the manifest-declared tile entry, if any).

Where the catalog engine ADDS value without risk (version semver, minRuntime), an unpacked dev folder shouldn't be blocked — dev iteration on a worktree is the whole point. But the ticket explicitly says "the shared widget validator... the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads". Since #1614 doesn't exist here, I define the shared validator now as a reusable class that BOTH the unpacked loader (this ticket) and future storage reads (#1614 parity) use: `WidgetPayloadValidator` in `flutter_app/lib/apps/widget_payload_validator.dart`? Hmm — but where would #1614's storage reads live? "the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads" — storage reads in the extension context = reading `apps/<id>/` from OPFS. In THIS repo's shape that's AppsStore.listApps / boot. The validator being "shared" means one Dart class both call.

Design: `flutter_app/lib/apps/widget_validator.dart`:
```dart
class WidgetPayloadIssue { final String code; final String message; }
class WidgetPayloadValidator {
  // validates a files-map payload {relPath: bytes} against the widget contract:
  // manifest.json present + parses (WidgetManifest.fromJson — shared engine), 
  // id matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$, widget.js present + non-empty,
  // declared tile entry present, size caps.
  static ValidatedWidgetPayload? validate(Map<String, Uint8List> files)
}
```
Pure Dart (no dart:io) — works on web + VM, fully unit-testable (UT-*). Uses `fa_widgets_tool`'s `WidgetManifest` parser (the shared schema engine) but NOT the directory-walking validator (dart:io, folder-name rule — wrong for unpacked). This is honest: schema errors byte-identical with CI ('x' must be a non-empty string), id regex identical to CI's (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}`), entry presence CI-equivalent.

Should I ALSO run the full catalog engine on VM for parity (like publish does)? That would reject version "1.0" (not strict semver) and folder-name mismatches — hostile to the dev-loop use case. I'll document the delta: unpacked validates the RUNTIME contract (what boot needs), not the catalog submission contract. And `WidgetPublishService` remains the catalog-identical path for publishing. This is a key decision for response.md.

Hmm wait — but what about `id == folder name` for the DESTINATION? The destination `apps/<id>` is derived from manifest.id, so no mismatch possible.

### Now `installWidget` origin parameter
`AppsStore.installWidget({required id, required version, required files})` hardcodes origin 'catalog'. I'll add `String origin = 'catalog'` param... wait, but `installedCatalogVersions()` filters `origin == 'catalog'`, `isCatalogInstalled` checks containsKey (any origin!). Hmm: `isCatalogInstalled` is used by publish flows to exclude catalog widgets from publishing. An unpacked widget should also be excluded from publishing? Publishing requires catalog meta... The publish sheet is offered for `!app.bundled` — including unpacked widgets. Publishing an unpacked widget would go through the standard pre-flight; that's the user's choice — fine, leave it.

Also `availableUpdates` / auto-update: `autoUpdateCleanWidgets` uses `installedCatalogVersions()` (origin=='catalog') so unpacked widgets never auto-update from the catalog. 

But careful — AC4: "catalog install works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation". What if an unpacked load REPLACES a catalog install (same id)? Then origin flips to 'unpacked' — catalog updates stop applying, correct (the user's local copy owns it now).

`isCleanInstall` — used by auto-update for catalog widgets; works on any meta entry. With origin recorded, `autoUpdateCleanWidgets` presumably iterates `installedCatalogVersions()` — let me verify catalog_auto_update.dart quickly.

### JsAppInfo install source surfacing
Add `installSource` field? listApps would need to read `.installed.json` origins — it already reads installed meta for prune. I'll attach `installSource` in listApps (from meta origin, null when not recorded — agent-created apps have none... wait `installedMetaFile` entries: putIfAbsent on install; agent-created apps aren't in meta at all). So: `String? installSource` on JsAppInfo ('catalog' | 'unpacked' | null).

## Implementation plan (TDD)

### Files to create

1. **`flutter_app/lib/apps/widget_payload_validator.dart`** — the shared widget validator:
   - `WidgetPayloadIssue` (code + message)
   - `ValidatedWidget` (id, name, version, manifest raw, entry bytes?, network flag, allowedCommands, tile entry)
   - `WidgetPayloadValidator.validate(Map<String, int-or-Uint8List> files)` → `WidgetPayloadValidation` (issues: errors/warnings, manifest).
   - Rules:
     - `manifest.json` exists in payload → else error `manifest_missing` "manifest.json not found in the folder".
     - Manifest parses as JSON object → else `manifest_malformed` "manifest.json is not valid JSON: …" / "manifest.json must be a JSON object".
     - Schema via `WidgetManifest.fromJson` (shared engine, byte-identical errors: "'id' must be a non-empty string") → `manifest_invalid`.
     - id regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` → error `id_invalid` naming the id and required pattern (CI-identical string: "manifest id 'X' must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}").
     - entry `widget.js` present and non-empty → `entry_missing` "widget.js not found in the folder" / `entry_empty`.
     - declared tile entry (`widget.entry`) present → `tile_entry_missing` (naming the file).
     - icon file declared → must be present → `icon_missing`? The catalog engine errors on a missing declared icon. For unpacked, missing icon = fallback glyph — but staying validator-shared: icon errors are cheap to include... Actually keep the runtime contract minimal but include icon presence since AppIcon renders it. Hmm — AppIcon handles a missing icon gracefully (fallback). I'll make icon missing a WARNING, not an error (dev-loop friendliness). Wait — what does the catalog engine do? `_validateIcon` — errors when declared icon missing (I saw `error(` at line 223 call — need to check severity). Let me not over-think: warning for unpacked (it's cosmetic), documenting the delta.
     - Size caps (loader-level, E4): per-file > 2 MiB → error `file_too_large` naming file + cap; total > 10 MiB → `package_too_large`.
   - Traversal: id regex already forbids `/`, `.`, `..`. Also file paths: reject any path with `..` segments or absolute paths → `path_unsafe` (defense in depth — root clamping per #1614).

   Pure Dart, no dart:io → runs on web + VM + in plain `flutter test`.

2. **`flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`** — the load pipeline over `ExecutionEnv`:
   ```dart
   class UnpackedWidgetLoader {
     UnpackedWidgetLoader({required ExecutionEnv env, AppsStore? appsStore});
     Future<UnpackedInspection> inspect(Map<String, Uint8List> files);
     // inspect: normalize paths (strip common root), validate → issues
     Future<void> install(UnpackedInspection inspection, {required String origin = 'unpacked'});
     // install: AppsStore.installWidget(origin: 'unpacked') — write-verified, all-or-nothing
   }
   class UnpackedInspection { id, name, version, manifest, files, issues, network, allowedCommands, replacesExisting (Future at UI level) }
   ```

Interesting — `WidgetManifest.fromJson` in this pinned fa_widgets version REQUIRES `minRuntime` to be a non-empty string! Wait, looking at the manifest.dart source I read earlier: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — `stringField` has `required_ = true` default... so minRuntime IS required in this version. Hmm wait — in the source I read: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — yes with default required_=true. So a manifest without minRuntime → "'minRuntime' must be a non-empty string".

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern). 

Also test line 173 failed: `validate({'id': id...})` for bad ids — wait, line 173 is inside 'bad ids are rejected': expect contains('id_invalid')... Actually the failure output above shows line 173:7 and 267/273 (the warnings group: `iconless` and `loose` versions). The minRuntime issue affects tests where the manifest parses but lacks minRuntime → manifest_invalid error → isValid false.

Fix in validator: in `_checkSchema`, build the stamped manifest first (minRuntime fallback), like WidgetPublishService.stampedManifest. I'll add a local stamp: `{...manifest, 'minRuntime': nonEmpty ?? '0.4.79'}` — better to reference WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime to keep one constant... that imports widget_publish_service.dart (which imports dart:io!). dart:io on web compiles (the app builds for web with it) — but importing dart:io into the validator would make IT dart:io-dependent. The publish service imports it already and the app builds — fine on both, but cleaner to keep the validator dart:io-free. I'll define the floor constant in the validator and have... no — duplicating constants is drift. WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'. The validator can define `catalogFloorRuntime` itself and publish could import it... don't touch publish (scope creep). I'll just reference the literal in the validator with a comment pointing at the publish constant. Hmm — actually let me check if the minRuntime requirement is version-specific and whether stamping is what publish does — yes: `stampedManifest` with `catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'`.

Cleaner: export the constant from the validator and leave publish alone (its own copy stays, one-line note). Fine.

Interesting — `WidgetManifest.fromJson` in this pinned fa_widgets version REQUIRES `minRuntime` to be a non-empty string! Hmm wait — in the source I read: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — yes with default required_=true. So a manifest without minRuntime → "'minRuntime' must be a non-empty string".

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern). 

Also test line 173 failed: `validate({'id': id...})` for bad ids — wait, line 173 is inside 'bad ids are rejected': expect contains('id_invalid')... Actually the failure output above shows line 173:7 and 267/273 (the warnings group: `iconless` and `loose` versions). The minRuntime issue affects tests where the manifest parses but lacks minRuntime → manifest_invalid error → isValid false.

Fix in validator: in `_checkSchema`, build the stamped manifest first (minRuntime fallback), like WidgetPublishService.stampedManifest. I'll add a local stamp: `{...manifest, 'minRuntime': nonEmpty ?? '0.4.79'}` — better to reference WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime to keep one constant... that imports widget_publish_service.dart (which imports dart:io!). dart:io on web compiles (the app builds for web with it) — but importing dart:io into the validator would make IT dart:io-dependent. The publish service imports it already and the app builds — fine on both, but cleaner to keep the validator dart:io-free. I'll define the floor constant in the validator and have... no — duplicating constants is drift. WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'. The validator can define `catalogFloorRuntime` itself and publish could import it... don't touch publish (scope creep). I'll just reference the literal in the validator with a comment pointing at the publish constant. Hmm — actually let me check if the minRuntime requirement is version-specific and whether stamping is what publish does — yes: `stampedManifest` with `catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'`.

Cleaner: export the constant from the validator and leave publish alone (its own copy stays, one-line note). Fine.

Interesting — `WidgetManifest.fromJson` in this pinned fa_widgets version REQUIRES `minRuntime` to be a non-empty string! Wait, looking at the manifest.dart source I read earlier: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — `stringField` has `required_ = true` default... so minRuntime IS required in this version. Hmm wait — in the source I read: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — yes with default required_=true. So a manifest without minRuntime → "'minRuntime' must be a non-empty string".

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern).

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern).

      ? this

          id: id,
          name: name,
          description: description,
          icon: icon,
          declaredPermissions: declaredPermissions,
          nameText: nameText,
          descriptionText: descriptionText,
          version: version,
          chrome: chrome,
          tileWidget: tileWidget,
          bundled: bundled,
          platforms: platforms,
          dirOverride: dirOverride,

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern).

messages.preview: The pinned catalog engine requires `minRuntime` — the publish flow stamps a floor before validating (`stampedManifest`). The loader must do the same:

blocks.text:
Interesting — `WidgetManifest.fromJson` in this pinned fa_widgets version REQUIRES `minRuntime` to be a non-empty string! Wait, looking at the manifest.dart source I read earlier: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — `stringField` has `required_ = true` default... so minRuntime IS required in this version. Hmm wait — in the source I read: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — yes with default required_=true. So a manifest without minRuntime → "'minRuntime' must be a non-empty string".

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern). 

Also test line 173 failed: `validate({'id': id...})` for bad ids — wait, line 173 is inside 'bad ids are rejected': expect contains('id_invalid')... Interesting — `WidgetManifest.fromJson` in this pinned fa_widgets version REQUIRES `minRuntime` to be a non-empty string! Wait, looking at the manifest.dart source I read earlier: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — `stringField` has `required_ = true` default... so minRuntime IS required in this version. Hmm wait — in the source I read: `final minRuntime = stringField('minRuntime');` — yes with default required_=true. So a manifest without minRuntime → "'minRuntime' must be a non-empty string".

Hmm, but catalog widgets ship minRuntime. And the app's own apps (agent-created) don't have minRuntime in their manifests... For the unpacked loader (dev worktrees!), requiring minRuntime is hostile. The publish service stamps minRuntime before validating (`stampedManifest`). 

Decision: the loader follows the same pattern — stamp `minRuntime` with the catalog floor ('0.4.79', same constant as WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime) BEFORE schema-parsing when missing/empty. That mirrors publish pre-flight exactly ("the manifest you publish" pattern). 

Also test line 173 failed: `validate({'id': id...})` for bad ids — wait, line 173 is inside 'bad ids are rejected': expect contains('id_invalid')... Actually the failure output above shows line 173:7 and 267/273 (the warnings group: `iconless` and `loose` versions). The minRuntime issue affects tests where the manifest parses but lacks minRuntime → manifest_invalid error → isValid false.

Fix in validator: in `_checkSchema`, build the stamped manifest first (minRuntime fallback), like WidgetPublishService.stampedManifest. I'll add a local stamp: `{...manifest, 'minRuntime': nonEmpty ?? '0.4.79'}` — better to reference WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime to keep one constant... that imports widget_publish_service.dart (which imports dart:io!). dart:io on web compiles (the app builds for web with it) — but importing dart:io into the validator would make IT dart:io-dependent. The publish service imports it already and the app builds — fine on both, but cleaner to keep the validator dart:io-free. I'll define the floor constant in the validator and have... no — duplicating constants is drift. WidgetPublishService.catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'. The validator can define `catalogFloorRuntime` itself and publish could import it... don't touch publish (scope creep). I'll just reference the literal in the validator with a comment pointing at the publish constant. Hmm — actually let me check if the minRuntime requirement is version-specific and whether stamping is what publish does — yes: `stampedManifest` with `catalogFloorRuntime = '0.4.79'`.

Cleaner: export the constant from the validator and leave publish alone (its own copy stays, one-line note). Fine.

Flow:
1. `final folderPicker = picker ?? createFolderPicker();` if null → return.
2. pick → files; empty → return (E1: cancelled/vanished → no-op).
3. inspect.

5. existing app check: listApps from store; find id == inspection.id → replace=true.
6. confirm dialog: UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog — icon+name+version+id, network row (if network), commands row (if any), replace warning (if replace) → returns bool. Buttons: Cancel / Load (or Replace).
7. install → fsRevision bump → success snack. Errors → error snack (l10n).

The web-picker test's manifest lacks `version`: `{'id': 'fa-agents', 'name': 'FA Agents'}`. So the engine requires version. The minimal valid manifest needs version. Two options: stamp a version default too, or fix the test. The engine REQUIRES version — catalog parity — an unpacked manifest without a version: JsAppInfo defaults '1.0.0' and everything works. Is requiring version right for unpacked? A dev worktree missing version is plausible. Hmm — the publish preflight requires version? `stampedManifest` only stamps minRuntime — version stays required there (publish needs semver for the release). For unpacked, booting needs no version.

Decision: stamp a default version too ('0.0.0') when missing/empty, with a warning (`version_missing`). This keeps the loader dev-friendly and the schema parse shared. Add to _checkSchema: if version missing/empty → warning + stamp '0.0.0'.

```dart
Future<void> loadUnpackedWidget(
  BuildContext context, {
  required FlutterSessionManager manager,

})
```

Flow:
1. `final folderPicker = picker ?? createFolderPicker();` if null → return.
2. pick → files; empty → return (E1: cancelled/vanished → no-op).
3. inspect.
4. !isValid → showDialog UnpackedLoadIssuesDialog (title, list of errors verbatim, copyable — follow guardBrokenApp's dialog style) → return.
5. existing app check: listApps from store; find id == inspection.id → replace=true.
6. confirm dialog: UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog — icon+name+version+id, network row (if network), commands row (if any), replace warning (if replace) → returns bool. Buttons: Cancel / Load (or Replace).
7. install → fsRevision bump → success snack. Errors → error snack (l10n).

Widgets: make the dialog widgets public classes in the same file (golden coverage).

85 passed. Now the UI flow (`unpacked_load_flow.dart`), the folder picker, launcher + apps panel entries, and l10n keys. Let me write the flow widget file. Design:

```dart
Future<void> loadUnpackedWidget(
  BuildContext context, {
  required FlutterSessionManager manager,
  AppsStore? appsStore,
  FolderPicker? picker,
  UnpackedWidgetLoader? loader,
})
```

Flow:
1. `final folderPicker = picker ?? createFolderPicker();` if null → return.
2. pick → files; empty → return (E1: cancelled/vanished → no-op).
3. inspect.
4. !isValid → showDialog UnpackedLoadIssuesDialog (title, list of errors verbatim, copyable — follow guardBrokenApp's dialog style) → return.
5. existing app check: listApps from store; find id == inspection.id → replace=true.
6. confirm dialog: UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog — icon+name+version+id, network row (if network), commands row (if any), replace warning (if replace) → returns bool. Buttons: Cancel / Load (or Replace).
7. install → fsRevision bump → success snack. Errors → error snack (l10n).

Widgets: make the dialog widgets public classes in the same file (golden coverage).

l10n keys needed (en + ru):
- unpackedLoadTitle: 'Load unpacked widget' / 'Загрузить распакованный виджет'
- unpackedLoadConfirmLoad: 'Load' / 'Загрузить'
- unpackedLoadConfirmReplace: 'Replace' / 'Заменить'
- unpackedLoadIdLabel — 'id' is just 'id'... Text('id: $id')? l10n-guard flags Text with letters: 'id: ...' contains letters → flagged! Route through l10n: unpackedLoadIdLine(id): 'id: {id}' / 'id: {id}'.
- unpackedLoadNetworkNote: 'This widget declares network access — it can fetch any origin.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadCommandsNote(commands): 'Shell commands it may run: {commands}.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadReplaceNote(source, version): 'A widget with this id already exists (installed from {source}, v{version}). Replacing overwrites the code; its saved data (storage.json) is kept.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadErrorTitle: 'Widget not loaded' / 'Виджет не загружен'
- unpackedLoadDone(name): '{name} loaded from the folder' / ru.
- unpackedLoadFailed(error): 'Load failed: {error}' / ru.

Flow:
1. `final folderPicker = picker ?? createFolderPicker();` if null → return.
2. pick → files; empty → return (E1: cancelled/vanished → no-op).
3. inspect.
4. !isValid → showDialog UnpackedLoadIssuesDialog (title, list of errors verbatim, copyable — follow guardBrokenApp's dialog style) → return.
5. existing app check: listApps from store; find id == inspection.id → replace=true.
6. confirm dialog: UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog — icon+name+version+id, network row (if network), commands row (if any), replace warning (if replace) → returns bool. Buttons: Cancel / Load (or Replace).
7. install → fsRevision bump → success snack. Errors → error snack (l10n).

Widgets: make the dialog widgets public classes in the same file (golden coverage).

```dart
Future<void> loadUnpackedWidget(
  BuildContext context, {
  required FlutterSessionManager manager,
  AppsStore? appsStore,
  FolderPicker? picker,

})

Flow:
1. `final folderPicker = picker ?? createFolderPicker();` if null → return.
2. pick → files; empty → return (E1: cancelled/vanished → no-op).
3. inspect.
4. !isValid → showDialog UnpackedLoadIssuesDialog (title, list of errors verbatim, copyable — follow guardBrokenApp's dialog style) → return.
5. existing app check: listApps from store; find id == inspection.id → replace=true.
6. confirm dialog: UnpackedLoadConfirmDialog — icon+name+version+id, network row (if network), commands row (if any), replace warning (if replace) → returns bool. Buttons: Cancel / Load (or Replace).
7. install → fsRevision bump → success snack. Errors → error snack (l10n).

l10n keys needed (en + ru):
- unpackedLoadTitle: 'Load unpacked widget' / 'Загрузить распакованный виджет'
- unpackedLoadConfirmLoad: 'Load' / 'Загрузить'

- unpackedLoadNetworkNote: 'This widget declares network access — it can fetch any origin.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadCommandsNote(commands): 'Shell commands it may run: {commands}.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadReplaceNote(source, version): 'A widget with this id already exists (installed from {source}, v{version}). Replacing overwrites the code; its saved data (storage.json) is kept.' / ru.
- unpackedLoadErrorTitle: 'Widget not loaded' / 'Виджет не загружен'
- unpackedLoadDone(name): '{name} loaded from the folder' / ru.
- unpackedLoadFailed(error): 'Load failed: {error}' / ru.

'')` — existingVersion comes from `existingApp?.version` = the MANIFEST-parsed version '1.0.0', not the meta '2.0.0'! So the note says v1.0.0, and my expect('2.0.0') fails. In the real AC4 test the same thing happened (the widget.js there is 'catalog' — manifest name 'Catalog version' v default 1.0.0 → note 'v1.0.0').

Which version is the honest one to show? The EXISTING install's version as recorded in meta (2.0.0) vs manifest (1.0.0). For "what am I replacing", the meta version is the install record; the manifest version is what's on disk. For catalog installs they agree. I'd use the manifest version (what listApps surfaces everywhere — the version map in the catalog sheet also uses app.version). So fix the TEST to expect the manifest-visible truth: name the existing app by name + source. I'll assert `find.textContaining('catalog')` and `find.textContaining('1.0.0')`... hmm wait — actually showing the meta version is MORE accurate for "the install being replaced"... The catalog sheet's Update button compares `_installed` versions read from listApps (`app.version` — manifest). So manifest version is the app-wide convention. Keep flow as-is; fix the test to assert on the source word + the version as surfaced (1.0.0). Hmm — but that reads weird ("replacing v1.0.0" while the catalog install recorded 2.0.0).

Cleaner: seed the EXISTING app's manifest with version 2.0.0 in the test (realistic — a catalog install writes the manifest WITH version). Then existingVersion = '2.0.0' and the note names it. Update the test manifest to include 'version': '2.0.0'.

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:

    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:

    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:

    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:

    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')

{"command":"cd flutter_app && python3 - <<'EOF'
import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}

import zlib, struct

def png_stats(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    # parse IHDR
    assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', 'not a png'
    w, h = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
    # collect all IDAT
    idat = b''
    i = 8
    while i < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
        typ = data[i+4:i+8]
        if typ == b'IDAT':
            idat += data[i+8:i+8+ln]
        i += 12 + ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    bpp = 4  # assume RGBA8
    stride = w * bpp + 1
    px = 0
    colors = set()
    minv, maxv = 255, 0
    sample = 0
    for y in range(0, h, 7):
        row = raw[y*stride+1:(y+1)*stride]
        # unfilter not needed for variance estimate: count distinct byte values
        for x in range(0, len(row), 40):
            b = row[x]
            colors.add(b)
            minv = min(minv, b); maxv = max(maxv, b)
            sample += 1
    return w, h, len(colors), minv, maxv, sample

for name in ['unpacked_load_confirm_network', 'unpacked_load_confirm_replace', 'unpacked_load_issues']:
    w, h, distinct, mn, mx, n = png_stats(f'test/golden/goldens/{name}.png')
    verdict = 'RICH' if distinct > 30 else 'SUSPICIOUS-FLAT'
    print(f'{name}: {w}x{h} distinct-bytes={distinct} range=[{mn},{mx}] samples={n} -> {verdict}')
EOF"}
